title: Cartwise Grocery Orders: Calculating the Wrong-Item Refund
content:
**Cartwise Grocery Orders — the wrong-item refund on a line whose substitution the customer approved.**

## Definition

1. **Wrong-item value.** The wrong-item value is the line's billed charge, that is the sum of the amounts billed on the line whose substitution the customer approved.
2. **Wrong-item keep share.** The wrong-item keep share is 40 percent.
3. **Wrong-item refund.** The wrong-item refund is the wrong-item value times the wrong-item keep share, rounded to the cent (half up) once.
4. **Ceiling.** The refund booked never exceeds the line's billed charge less the wrong-item refunds already standing on the order, and that ceiling is never below zero.

## Where each figure is read

| Quantity | Record it comes from |
|---|---|
| Line's billed charge | The billed item line entries of the line whose substitution decision is approved by the customer, amounts summed |
| Wrong-item refunds already standing | The item refund entries on the order carrying the wrong item reason, amounts summed |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A hypothetical approved-replacement line is billed 12.35 in total, and no wrong-item refund stands on the order.

- Wrong-item value: 12.35.
- Keep share: 40 percent.
- 12.35 multiplied by 40 percent is 4.94, which is already a whole number of cents.
- Ceiling: 12.35 less nothing already refunded, so 12.35; 4.94 lies below it.
- **Wrong-item refund: 4.94.**

A second hypothetical line billed 7.99: 7.99 multiplied by 40 percent is 3.196, which rounds half up to **3.20**.

## Ceiling in practice (hypothetical)

If a hypothetical wrong-item refund of 10.00 already stood on an order whose approved-replacement line was billed 12.35, the ceiling would be 12.35 less 10.00, that is 2.35, and no refund booked on the line could exceed 2.35.
